question_text: Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = x³ + 4x² at (−1, 3).

mark_split.label: Differentiate and find the slope at (−1, 3)

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what dy/dx is, what care the negative x-coordinate needs, and how the normal's slope follows from the tangent's.

steps.label: Differentiate and find the slope at (−1, 3)
steps.margin_note: Two marks: one for dy/dx = 3x² + 8x, one for its value at x = −1. Write the powers of −1 out in full — (−1)² is +1 and (−1)³ is −1, and mixing those two is the commonest slip in this question.
lines: Check the point: at x = −1,  y = (−1)³ + 4(−1)² = −1 + 4 = 3,

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx = 3x² + 8x, and putting x = −1 gives m = −5.
accept: differentiate to three x squared plus eight x
put x equal to minus one to get three minus eight
the slope of the tangent is minus five
minus one square plus one, minus one cube minus one
x equal to minus one pettite minus five vasthundi
check first that minus one gives y equal to three
heard_as: three x squared plus eight x

steps.why: An even power of a negative number is positive and an odd power is negative, so 3(−1)² stays +3 while 8(−1) becomes −8. Writing both substitutions out keeps the two signs separate.
common_mistakes: Writing 3(−1)² as −3, applying the minus sign to the squared term.
Getting m = 3 + 8 = 11 by taking 8(−1) as positive.
steps.memory_tip: Even power of a negative is positive, odd power is negative. (−1)² = 1 and (−1)³ = −1.

steps.label: Equation of the tangent
steps.margin_note: Third mark. x₁ = −1, so (x − x₁) becomes (x + 1). Two minus signs together make a plus — write the bracket out before expanding it.
lines: Tangent at (x₁, y₁) with slope m:   y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

recall.must_convey: That the point-slope form with (−1, 3) and m = −5 gives 5x + y + 2 = 0.
accept: x minus minus one becomes x plus one
y minus three equals minus five into x plus one
the tangent is five x plus y plus two equals zero
minus minus one ante plus one
expand minus five into x plus one to get minus five x minus five
collect everything on the left side

steps.why: The point-slope form subtracts x₁, and x₁ is itself negative, so the bracket becomes a sum. Collecting −3 and −5 gives the constant +2 once every term moves to the left.
common_mistakes: Writing the bracket as (x − 1) instead of (x + 1).
Ending at 5x + y − 2 = 0, losing the sign of the constant.
steps.memory_tip: x minus a negative is x plus. Write (x − (−1)) in full for one line before simplifying it to (x + 1).

steps.label: Equation of the normal
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. m = −5 is negative, so −1/m = +1/5. Check the boxed normal at (−1, 3): −1 − 15 + 16 = 0.
lines: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at the same point,

recall.must_convey: That the normal's slope is 1/5, giving x − 5y + 16 = 0.
accept: the normal slope is minus one by minus five which is one by five
the two minus signs cancel so the slope is positive
the normal is x minus five y plus sixteen equals zero
minus one by minus five ante one by five
multiply by five to clear the fraction
the normal passes through minus one comma three too

steps.why: The tangent's slope is negative, so the negative reciprocal is positive: the two lines lean opposite ways through the point. Collecting −15 and −1 gives the constant +16 after every term moves to the left.
common_mistakes: Writing the normal's slope as −1/5 and keeping a minus that has already cancelled.
Using 5 as the normal's slope, changing the sign but not inverting.
Arithmetic slip on −15 − 1, giving +14 or −14 instead of +16.
steps.memory_tip: Minus one divided by a negative slope is positive. A tangent sloping down has a normal sloping up.

insider_note: Check the point is on the curve first, then m = 3x² + 8x at x = −1 gives −5. Watch the signs: squaring −1 gives +1 while the linear term stays negative.
